text: Go outside or to the window and find 3 different leaves.
hook: Did you know every tree has leaves with different shapes? Let's discover how many shapes you can find!

text: Find 5 objects at home that start with the letter C.
hook: The letter C is hiding in lots of words around you. Can a letter hunter find them all?

text: Measure the kitchen table with your own steps. How many steps is it?
hook: Before rulers existed, people measured everything with their bodies! Let's be old-school explorers?

text: Put an ice cube on a plate. How long does it take to melt?
hook: Ice is water that got very cold. How long do you think it takes to turn back into water?

text: Look for the Moon in the sky tonight. What shape is it?
hook: The Moon changes shape through the month, like it's always changing outfits. What shape is it tonight?

text: At the supermarket, find something that costs less than 2€.
hook: Learning the value of money starts with looking at prices. Do you think it's easy to find something that cheap?

text: Sort the clean laundry socks by color.
hook: Sorting by color trains your eye to spot patterns, just like a real detective!

text: Sit by the window for 5 minutes. How many birds can you see?
hook: There are hundreds of kinds of birds in the world. How many can you spot right on your street?

text: Pick a book and find 3 words you already know how to read.
hook: Reading is like opening a magic door to other worlds. How many words can you already open on your own?

text: Help fold 5 pieces of clothing.
hook: Folding clothes is a puzzle of shapes and sizes. Can you make neat, tidy piles?

text: Draw an animal that doesn't exist yet. Give it a name!
hook: Every animal that exists started as an idea. What if you invented the next one?

text: Do 10 jumps, then walk like a crab all the way to the door.
hook: Moving your body in different ways helps your brain grow sharper. Let's give it a try!

text: Run and find 3 red things at home.
hook: Red is one of the first colors your eyes notice. How many red things are there at home?

text: Clap a rhythm with your hands. Can someone at home repeat it?
hook: Music begins with simple sound patterns. Can you create a rhythm no one can copy?

text: Build a paper or cardboard bridge between two chairs.
hook: Engineers always test their ideas before building real bridges. Let's be engineers today!

text: In the bath, find 3 objects that float and 3 that sink.
hook: Not everything heavy sinks, and not everything light floats. Let's investigate why!

text: Ask a grandparent what games they played when they were little.
hook: Before phones existed, people invented amazing games. Discover a story from your family!

text: Pack your own school bag for tomorrow, all by yourself.
hook: Organizing your own things is a superpower that helps you every day. Let's practice!

text: Prepare a simple snack (e.g. a sandwich) with an adult's help.
hook: Preparing food is a mix of science and art. Let's create something delicious together!

text: Help set the table and count how many spoons and forks are needed.
hook: Counting everyday objects is math hiding everywhere. Help set the table and count!

text: Plant a seed in a cup of soil and water it. Watch it every day.
hook: Inside a tiny seed, a whole plant is hiding. Let's help it grow!

text: Practice tying your shoelaces by yourself.
hook: Tying shoelaces seems hard, but with practice your hands learn on their own. Let's train!

text: Lie on the grass or sit by the window and watch the clouds for 5 minutes. What shapes can you see?
hook: Clouds keep changing shape, like a picture book in the sky. What do you see today?

text: With an adult near a street, count how many red cars pass by in 5 minutes.
hook: Counting and sorting things helps your brain organize the world. How many red cars pass by?

text: Ask someone in your family to teach you one new word in a different language.
hook: Every language is a different way of seeing the world. What new word will you discover today?

text: Make a paper airplane and test how far it can fly. Try to improve it!
hook: The first real airplane also began with lots of tries. Can you make yours fly farther?

text: With an adult, sort the household trash into the right recycling bins: paper, plastic and glass.
hook: Sorting trash is a way to take care of the planet every day. Do you know which bin each thing belongs in?

text: Write or draw a thank-you note for someone special and give it to them.
hook: A simple written thank-you can give someone a huge smile. Who will you write to?

text: On a sunny day, trace the outline of your shadow on the ground with chalk. How does it change during the day?
hook: Your shadow moves through the day because the Sun changes position in the sky. Let's see how it changes!

text: On a walk, find signs or shop names with 5 different letters of the alphabet.
hook: Letters are scattered all over the street, on signs and shop names. Can you find them all?

text: Count the coins you find in a piggy bank or drawer. How much money is that in total?
hook: Counting coins helps you understand how money works. How much do you think you'll find?

text: Jump rope 20 times in a row without stopping. Can you beat your record tomorrow?
hook: Jumping rope trains your body and your focus at the same time. Can you make it to 20?

text: With an adult's help, make a musical instrument out of a bottle and rice or beans.
hook: Many musical instruments around the world were invented from simple materials. Let's make yours!

text: Build the tallest tower you can with plastic cups. How many did you use?
hook: Building tall towers teaches you about balance, just like building engineers. How high can you go?

text: Draw a treasure map of your house and hide a "treasure" for someone to find.
hook: Maps have helped explorers find amazing places for centuries. What treasure will you hide?

text: Help an adult prepare a simple recipe and count how many ingredients you used.
hook: Cooking is a recipe of math, science and patience all mixed together. Let's count the ingredients!

text: Imitate the sound and movement of 5 different animals. Can someone guess which ones they are?
hook: Imitating animals helps you learn how they move and communicate. Who will you be first?

text: Count how many steps there are between two floors at home or in a building.
hook: Counting stairs is math you use every day without noticing. How many are there at your place?

text: With a flashlight and your hands, create 3 different shadows that look like animals.
hook: With your hands and a light, you can make shadows that look like real animals. Let's try it!

text: Ask an adult the name of 3 plants that grow near your home.
hook: Every plant has its own name, just like people do. How many can you discover around you?

text: Pick up 2 objects at home and guess which is heavier using only your hands.
hook: Can you tell which is heavier using only your hands, no scale? Let's test your sense of weight!

text: Write or draw a short letter for a family member who lives far away.
hook: A handwritten letter is a gift that gets kept forever. Who will you write to today?

text: Stack books to build the tallest, most stable tower you can.
hook: Stacking books carefully teaches you about balance and center of gravity. How high can you go?

text: Close your eyes for 1 minute and count how many different sounds you can hear at home.
hook: Close your eyes and listen: your home is full of sounds you don't usually notice. How many can you identify?

text: Pick any object in your house and invent a short story about it.
hook: Any object can be the start of an amazing story, if you use your imagination. Let's make one up!
